docs.title: Quick Start: Your First Parallel Algorithm
docs.text:
This walks through a complete multithreading program: a synthetic binary-tree traversal that counts leaves in parallel. It is a trimmed version of the benchmark from gempba-examples, and it uses the public API exactly as your own algorithm would. The same pattern works for any recursive branching algorithm.

First install GemPBA (see Installation). This example uses the core alone, so no MPI is needed.

docs.title: The shape of a GemPBA program
docs.text:
Every GemPBA program follows the same three beats:

  1. Set up a load balancer and a node manager, and configure the goal.
  2. Seed the recursion with a root node, then submit it.
  3. Wait for completion and read the result back.

Your algorithm is the recursive function in the middle. GemPBA owns the thread pool, the work queue, and the best-result bookkeeping.

docs.title: The recursive task
docs.text:
GemPBA inserts itself into your recursion through a small set of parameter additions. The recipe:

  1. Add std::thread::id as the first parameter and gempba::node as the last parameter of your function.
  2. Create a node for each branch inside the function.
  3. Submit one branch to the thread pool, forward the other on the current thread.
#include <gempba/gempba.hpp>

#include <atomic>

std::atomic<int> leaf_count{0};

// 1. std::thread::id first, gempba::node last; your arguments in between
void explore(std::thread::id tid, int depth, int max_depth, gempba::node parent) {
    gempba::node_manager& nm = gempba::get_node_manager();
    gempba::load_balancer& lb = *gempba::get_load_balancer();

    if (depth == max_depth) {                       // leaf: record a result
        int count = ++leaf_count;
        nm.try_update_result(count, gempba::score::make(count));
        return;
    }

    // The seed arrives with no parent; substitute a dummy so children
    // always have an anchor in the tree
    gempba::node effective_parent = parent == nullptr ? gempba::create_dummy_node(lb) : parent;

    // 2. Create a node per branch. Template arguments: <Ret, Args...>,
    //    where Args are your parameters minus the thread id and the node.
    gempba::node left = gempba::create_explicit_node<void, int, int>(
        lb, effective_parent, &explore, std::make_tuple(depth + 1, max_depth));
    gempba::node right = gempba::create_explicit_node<void, int, int>(
        lb, effective_parent, &explore, std::make_tuple(depth + 1, max_depth));

    // 3. Hand one child to the pool, keep walking the other on this thread
    nm.try_local_submit(left);
    nm.forward(right);
}

The try_local_submit / forward pair is the idiom: offer one branch to the thread pool, recurse into the other yourself. The quasi-horizontal load balancer decides which pending work is most valuable to hand out.

docs.title: The driver
docs.text:
#include <iostream>
#include <stdexcept>

int main() {
    constexpr int MAX_DEPTH = 16;   // 2^16 = 65,536 leaves; raise it to make the machine sweat

    // 1. Set up
    gempba::load_balancer* lb = gempba::create_load_balancer(gempba::balancing_policy::QUASI_HORIZONTAL);
    gempba::node_manager& nm = gempba::create_node_manager(lb);

    nm.set_goal(gempba::MAXIMISE, gempba::score_type::I32);   // maximise an int score
    nm.set_thread_pool_size(8);
    nm.set_score(gempba::score::make(0));                     // initial score

    // 2. Seed the recursion from depth 0
    gempba::node seed = gempba::create_seed_node<void, int, int>(
        *lb, &explore, std::make_tuple(0, MAX_DEPTH));

    const double start = nm.get_wall_time();
    if (!nm.try_local_submit(seed)) {
        throw std::runtime_error("unable to submit seed node");
    }

    // 3. Wait and read results
    nm.wait();
    const double elapsed = nm.get_wall_time() - start;

    std::cout << "Score: " << nm.get_score().to_string() << '\n';
    std::cout << "Elapsed: " << elapsed << " s\n";
    std::cout << "Pool idle time: " << nm.get_idle_time() << " s\n";
    std::cout << "Thread requests: " << nm.get_thread_request_count() << '\n';

    return gempba::shutdown();
}

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
The two snippets above form a single main.cpp: the task first, the driver below it. Wire it into a CMake project (see Installation):

find_package(gempba REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE gempba::gempba)

Build, run, and watch all eight workers light up. For the full, runnable version of this program (with per-node cost simulation and benchmark plumbing), see multithreading/src/benchmark.cpp in gempba-examples.

To stop early, press Ctrl+C once: the run winds down gracefully and keeps the best result found so far. Stopping a Run covers the other ways to stop it and how a run says it ended.

docs.title: What changes for MPI
docs.text:
An MPI program keeps the same recursive-task shape and adds a scheduler from the MPI component:

  • It includes <gempba/mpi.hpp>, asks for the component with find_package(gempba REQUIRED COMPONENTS mpi), and links gempba::mpi.
  • gempba::mpi::create_scheduler(topology) comes first, and the load balancer and node manager factories take the scheduler: gempba::create_load_balancer(policy, scheduler), gempba::create_node_manager(lb, scheduler).
  • Node factories take a serializer / deserializer pair so a task's arguments can travel between ranks as a gempba::task_packet.
  • Every rank registers the same runnables and calls scheduler->run(nm, runnables, seed), which returns once the whole run has ended. Only the root, rank 0, passes the seed, and only the root reads the best result, with scheduler->get_result().
  • The program is launched under mpiexec.

See the multiprocessing tree in gempba-examples for a full MP program, and IPC Topologies for the scheduler layouts.

docs.title: v5.0.0
docs.text:
November 14, 2026

GitHub ↗

A breaking release. gempba becomes one library with multithreading built in, plus an MPI component that a program asks for when it needs it, so the build-time flavors and their two namespaces are gone. Every rank calls one entry point, scheduler::run, and a run can be stopped early, from code, by a signal or from a dashboard, and says how it ended. The MPI component compiles against the MPI on the user's machine, the Java artifacts move to Maven Central, and the JARs' macOS native is Apple Silicon. Everything v4.3.0 deprecated is removed.

Upgrading needs code and build changes. C++ programs drop the multithreading:: and multiprocessing:: qualifiers and GEMPBA_MULTIPROCESSING; MPI programs include <gempba/mpi.hpp>, create their scheduler with gempba::mpi::create_scheduler(topology), call scheduler::run on every rank and link gempba::mpi from find_package(gempba COMPONENTS mpi). C programs use the unprefixed calls and gempba_mpi.h, and Java programs depend on io.github.rapastranac:gempba or gempba-mpi. SIGINT and SIGTERM now stop a run gracefully instead of killing it; gempba::stop_on_signals(false) keeps the old behavior. Removed and Renamed list every change with what to use instead.

Removed

  • The build-time flavors. The GEMPBA_MULTIPROCESSING option and the compile definition it passed to consumers, the gempba::multithreading and gempba::multiprocessing namespaces, find_package(gempba COMPONENTS mt) and the rule that mt and mpi can't be used together are gone. Use find_package(gempba) and the calls in gempba, and add COMPONENTS mpi and gempba::mpi for MPI. Code that branched on GEMPBA_MULTIPROCESSING decides its mode itself (#414)
  • The build options GEMPBA_DEV_MODE and GEMPBA_INSTALL_SHARED_ARTIFACTS. Nothing replaces them: the test hooks follow GEMPBA_BUILD_TESTS, and each install component ships only its own files. GEMPBA_BUILD_MPI replaces GEMPBA_MULTIPROCESSING in gempba's own build (see Build) (#414)
  • The installed MPI library. libgempba_mpi.a, its CMake targets file and gempba-mpi.pc no longer install, since the MPI component installs as source (see Changed). An MPI program uses find_package(gempba COMPONENTS mpi); no pkg-config file describes it. gempba.pc describes the core and no longer sets -DGEMPBA_MULTIPROCESSING (#415, #414)
  • The scheduler's center and worker views. scheduler::center, scheduler::worker, center_view(), worker_view() and worker::next_process() are gone. Call scheduler::run(node_manager, runnables, seed) on every rank, with the seed on rank 0 only, and read get_result() and get_all_results() from scheduler on rank 0. force_push and try_open_transmission_channel move onto scheduler, and create_load_balancer, create_node_manager and node_traits::delegate_remotely take a scheduler* instead of a scheduler::worker* (#394)
  • The scheduler timeout, ignored since v4.3.0. create_scheduler(topology, timeout) → gempba::mpi::create_scheduler(topology), the C ABI's gempba_scheduler_create(topology, timeout, out) → gempba_mpi_create_scheduler(topology, out), and Java's GemPBA.createScheduler(topology, timeout) → io.gempba.mpi.Mpi.createScheduler(topology) (#353, #414)
  • The v4.3.0 deprecations (#373):
  • telemetry_hub::set_worker_interval_ms(), worker_interval_ms(), latest_worker_frame() and control_kind::SET_WORKER_INTERVAL_MS: use set_interval_ms(), interval_ms(), latest_rank_frame() and SET_INTERVAL_MS;
  • telemetry_hub::set_node_interval_ms(), which did nothing, and node_interval_ms(): node frames follow set_interval_ms() and interval_ms();
  • the set_worker_interval_ms and set_node_interval_ms control lines, now dropped as unknown: send {"kind":"set_interval_ms","value":N};
  • the total_requested_tasks stat, with default_mpi_stats_visitor::m_total_requested_tasks and its key in the C ABI's stats visit and Java's RankStats: read coordinator_messages_handled on the coordinator, and sent_task_count + received_task_count on workers.
  • The public telemetry transport. <gempba/telemetry/telemetry_transport.hpp> no longer installs, and with it telemetry_transport, worker_frame_sink, publish_worker and publish_final_worker. v5.0.0 publishes no backend or transport interface, and gempba::mpi is its only backend. A custom scheduler still plugs in through gempba::mpi::create_scheduler(std::unique_ptr<scheduler>), and gets telemetry over MPI (#414)
  • Java's Scheduler.Center and Scheduler.Worker, with Scheduler.center() and worker(). Call Scheduler.run(nm, runnables, seed, seedRunnableId) on rank 0 and run(nm, runnables) on the other ranks, and read getResult() and getAllResults() from Scheduler on rank 0 (#394)

Renamed

  • MPI's calls are in gempba::mpi, from <gempba/mpi.hpp> (#414):
  • create_scheduler(topology) and create_scheduler(std::unique_ptr<scheduler>) → gempba::mpi::create_scheduler;
  • scheduler_topology, CENTRALIZED and SEMI_CENTRALIZED → gempba::mpi::scheduler_topology, gempba::mpi::CENTRALIZED and gempba::mpi::SEMI_CENTRALIZED;
  • get_default_mpi_stats_visitor() → gempba::mpi::get_default_mpi_stats_visitor();
  • <gempba/defaults/default_mpi_stats_visitor.hpp> → <gempba/mpi/default_mpi_stats_visitor.hpp>, which <gempba/mpi.hpp> includes. The class stays gempba::default_mpi_stats_visitor.
  • Every other call is in gempba, in all its forms (#414, #394):
  • multithreading::create_load_balancer(policy) and multiprocessing::create_load_balancer(policy, worker) → gempba::create_load_balancer(policy, scheduler = nullptr);
  • multithreading::create_node_manager(lb) and multiprocessing::create_node_manager(lb, worker) → gempba::create_node_manager(lb, scheduler = nullptr);
  • the node factories (create_explicit_node and create_lazy_node, with and without serializers, and create_from_bytes_node) and runnables::return_none and runnables::return_value keep their names, in gempba.
  • Telemetry's C++ names say rank for a process, as schema 2's keys already do; the JSON doesn't change (#373):
  • worker_frame, worker_frame_header and worker_identity → rank_frame, rank_frame_header and rank_identity;
  • telemetry_hub::snapshot_worker_frame() → snapshot_rank_frame();
  • m_worker_id → m_rank, m_worker_local_ms → m_rank_local_ms, m_idle_microseconds_per_worker → m_idle_microseconds_per_thread, m_sentinel_worker_id → m_sentinel_rank, m_dst_worker_id → m_dst_rank, and the topology's m_worker_ids → m_ranks;
  • MAX_WORKERS → MAX_RANKS.
  • The C ABI drops the mt and mp prefixes (#414, #394):
  • gempba_mt_create_load_balancer and gempba_mp_create_load_balancer → gempba_create_load_balancer(policy, scheduler), and gempba_mt_create_node_manager and gempba_mp_create_node_manager → gempba_create_node_manager(lb, scheduler), with a NULL scheduler in a multithreading program;
  • gempba_mt_create_explicit_node and gempba_mp_create_explicit_node → gempba_create_explicit_node, whose nodes can be sent to other ranks, and gempba_mt_create_lazy_node → gempba_create_lazy_node;
  • gempba_scheduler_create → gempba_mpi_create_scheduler, in gempba_mpi.h with gempba_scheduler_topology_t;
  • the gempba_scheduler_center_* and gempba_scheduler_worker_* calls and their gempba_scheduler_center_t and gempba_scheduler_worker_t handles → gempba_scheduler_run, gempba_scheduler_is_root, gempba_scheduler_get_result and gempba_scheduler_visit_all_results, on the scheduler itself, where gempba_scheduler_barrier, gempba_scheduler_rank_me and gempba_scheduler_world_size already were.
  • Java (#414, #394):
  • io.gempba.scheduler.SchedulerTopology → io.gempba.mpi.SchedulerTopology, and GemPBA.createScheduler → io.gempba.mpi.Mpi.createScheduler;
  • GemPBA.createLoadBalancer(policy, Scheduler.Worker) and createNodeManager(lb, Scheduler.Worker) take the Scheduler.

Changed

  • One core library, with MPI as a component. libgempba (gempba::gempba) holds the nodes, the node manager, the load balancers, the thread pool, the scheduler interface, telemetry and the C ABI; the MPI schedulers and MPI telemetry are the MPI component, gempba::mpi. One program can link both, and multithreading and MPI programs build side by side from one installation (#414)
  • libgempba is a shared library, libgempba.so.5 on Linux and libgempba.dll on Windows, where v4 installed libgempba.a. It exports only its public API. spdlog and fmt are compiled into it, and hwloc is a private dependency it loads at run time, so find_package(gempba) looks only for the threads library and a consumer compiles against only the C++ standard library, plus MPI for gempba::mpi. Programs load it at run time, from where the packages install it with hwloc's runtime (#414)
  • The MPI component compiles against your MPI. It installs as source, and find_package(gempba COMPONENTS mpi) compiles it in your build into a static gempba::mpi, against the MPI CMake finds there: Open MPI, MPICH or MS-MPI. Before, each package's MPI part was compiled against one MPI and worked only with it. Your compiler must be compatible with the one that built libgempba, and switching MPIs takes another build directory, not a reinstall. A gempba build installs the component without MPI, and so does Homebrew; the apt and MSYS2 packages depend on an MPI (#415)
  • The packages keep their names, and each MPI package installs on top of its core package (#414, #415, #438):
  • apt: libgempba-dev is the core and depends on hwloc's runtime, libhwloc15, instead of libfmt-dev, libhwloc-dev and pkgconf. libgempba-mpi-dev holds the MPI component's source and depends on libopenmpi-dev (>= 4.0) | libmpich-dev. Ubuntu 24.04's MPICH package starts every rank of a job alone (Launchpad bug 2072338), so use Open MPI there;
  • Homebrew: gempba-mpi depends on gempba from the same tap instead of conflicting with it, so both install together, and holds only the MPI component's source; brew install open-mpi or mpich for your build to compile it against. gempba installs only the core;
  • MSYS2: mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gempba is the core and no longer depends on fmt or pkgconf; mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gempba-mpi holds the MPI component's source and depends on MS-MPI. Both are in MSYS2's own UCRT64 repository, so pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gempba installs gempba, and the .pkg.tar.zst files on the GitHub Release still install with pacman -U (#413).
  • One entry point on every rank. scheduler::run throws std::invalid_argument if rank 0 passes no seed or another rank passes one, and get_result() and get_all_results() throw std::logic_error off rank 0; is_root() tells a rank whether it is rank 0. The built-in schedulers keep rank 0 as their coordinator, out of compute. A custom scheduler implements the protected do_run, do_get_result and do_get_all_results. Each rank reports its own role_of(rank_me()) to telemetry at startup, so a role no longer has to be the same answer on every rank (#394)
  • SIGINT and SIGTERM stop a run gracefully by default, in C++ and Java, instead of killing it (see Added). create_node_manager takes each of the two signals that nothing else handles yet, and shutdown() gives them back, so a program that installed its own handler first keeps it. A second Ctrl+C kills the process, while SIGTERM stays handled. gempba::stop_on_signals(false), or Java's GemPBA.stopOnSignals(false), keeps the signals' default. In Java, GemPBA.createNodeManager takes both through sun.misc.Signal instead of letting the JVM shut down, and a second SIGINT goes to the JVM's own handler (#465)
  • The Java artifacts are on Maven Central as io.github.rapastranac:gempba (multithreading) and io.github.rapastranac:gempba-mpi, with no repository or token to configure. The Java packages stay io.gempba. v4.1.0 to v4.4.0 stay on GitHub Packages as io.gempba:gempba with the mt and mp-mpi classifiers, and GitHub Packages gets nothing from v5.0.0 on. build_jar_<os>.sh installs into ~/.m2 under the new coordinates (#410, #470)
  • One Java API for both artifacts. One GemPBA class serves both; io.gempba.mpi ships only in gempba-mpi, so MPI code doesn't compile against gempba (#414)
  • The JARs' macOS native is Apple Silicon only. Each JAR holds exactly the linux-x86_64, win-x86_64 and osx-aarch64 natives, where v4.3.0 and v4.4.0 shipped osx-x86_64. On an Intel Mac, build the native from your version's tag with bash scripts/build_jar_macos.sh MT (or MP) and pass it with -Dgempba.native.path=<checkout>/bindings/java/src/main/resources/natives/osx-x86_64/gempba_jni.dylib (#409)

Added

  • Stopping a run early (#465):
  • gempba::request_stop() asks the run to stop, from any thread, and returns at once. Nodes that haven't started are pruned, nodes already running finish their own work, and the run returns its best result so far, with its stats. The first stop wins until gempba::shutdown();
  • gempba::stop_requested() says whether a stop was requested; long work inside one node can poll it and return early. A multithreading run, which has no scheduler::run, checks it after wait() and before shutdown();
  • under MPI every rank stops, ranks that saw no signal too, and the run ends through the usual termination, result gathering and MPI_Finalize, without MPI_Abort;
  • scheduler::run returns a gempba::run_outcome, the same on every rank: m_reason (end_reason::COMPLETED or INTERRUPTED), m_trigger (stop_trigger::NONE, CODE, SIGNAL or CONTROL) and m_signal. A custom scheduler returns it from do_run, and docs/telemetry/custom-schedulers.md says what else it does on a stop;
  • C ABI: gempba_request_stop(), gempba_stop_requested(), gempba_stop_on_signals(), gempba_request_stop_on_signal() for a signal the host language caught itself, and gempba_scheduler_run fills a nullable gempba_run_outcome_t*;
  • Java: GemPBA.requestStop(), GemPBA.isStopRequested() and GemPBA.stopOnSignals(boolean), and Scheduler.run returns an io.gempba.value.RunOutcome with reason(), trigger(), signal() and isInterrupted().
  • A run says how it ended (#465):
  • rank 0 logs one line: gempba: run completed: the whole search space was explored, so the result is proven, or a warning such as gempba: run interrupted by SIGTERM: the result is the best one found before the stop, not a proven one, likewise by SIGINT (Ctrl+C), by gempba::request_stop() or from the dashboard. scheduler::run logs it, so custom schedulers get it too, and a run without a scheduler logs it in shutdown();
  • the final telemetry line carries end: {"reason":"completed"}, or for example {"reason":"interrupted","trigger":"signal","signal":"SIGTERM"}. A stream that closes without a final line was lost: killed by SIGKILL, a crash or a node failure. The schema stays 2.
  • A dashboard can stop the run with the control line {"kind":"stop","token":"…"}, accepted only when token matches the GEMPBA_STOP_TOKEN environment variable the run was started with; without that variable, every stop line is refused with a warning. Any user on the host can reach the telemetry socket, so the token keeps others from ending your run (#465)
  • Slurm jobs can end interrupted instead of lost. A time limit sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the cluster's KillWait, which may not leave the run time to wind down. Add #SBATCH --signal=TERM@<seconds>, with more seconds than your longest node takes, and start the ranks with srun, so every rank gets SIGTERM that long before the limit; --signal=B:TERM@… signals only the batch shell. scancel --signal=TERM <jobid> stops a job gracefully by hand (#465)
  • The JARs can load a native library you built. -Dgempba.native.path=<file> loads that file instead of the bundled one, and fails if it names no file. gempba-mpi's bundled native is built against Open MPI on Linux and macOS and MS-MPI on Windows; when it fails to load, the error keeps the OS's reason, names the MPI it was built against and points at gempba.native.path and the README's Which MPI section. The JNI build records that MPI in gempba_jni.properties, inside the JAR (#442)
  • scripts/build_jar_host_linux.sh MT|MP builds the JAR on a cluster, without Docker. It builds the static hwloc the native links, with fmt's and spdlog's headers, builds gempba_jni against the host's compiler and MPI, prints the MPI it found and installs the JAR into ~/.m2. Run it from the tag of your version, with a C++23 compiler, CMake, curl, Maven, a JDK and your MPI on PATH; it loads no modules (#446)

Fixed

  • Under the centralized MPI scheduler, rank 0's result could be empty although a worker had found the best one: a worker's last improvement, found by its last task, was never proposed to rank 0. The worker now proposes its score once more before going idle, as the semi-centralized worker does (#433)
  • An MPI worker could take tens of seconds to see the termination message. Both MPI schedulers probed one communicator until it was empty, so a backlog of score updates held the termination message back; they now take the communicators in turn (#465)
  • The quasi-horizontal balancer could run a branch twice, silently. A running branch's deep send could hand that same branch to another thread, since it stayed UNUSED while it ran. Nodes are now RUNNING while their runnable executes (node_state gains RUNNING), and the balancer hands off only the leftmost root child still UNUSED (#456)
  • Submitting a node the balancer had already dispatched no longer throws Node: N is already consumed. In both balancers, try_local_submit and try_remote_submit return true for a node already PUSHED, SENT_TO_ANOTHER_PROCESS or DISCARDED, as forward already skipped it (#456)
  • The quasi-horizontal balancer no longer throws Attempted to access a null node when it sends a root that still has children. After pruning a node with no parent, it went on to correct the root of that node's missing parent; it now stops there, as the work-stealing balancer does (#459)
  • A new load balancer no longer reports a full pool. For the first 100–200 µs, before its threads first went idle, a submission ran in the calling thread and counted as a pool-full rejection; both constructors now return once every thread is idle (#428)
  • Telemetry no longer slows each node's sentinel rank. The sentinel rebuilt the hwloc topology on every node frame, on its scheduler thread: 94–131 ms per frame on a cluster, about a fifth of the thread's time at the default 500 ms interval, which showed as jagged CPU on the dashboard. It now loads the topology once per run (#454)
  • Multi-node MPI runs over UCX no longer end with UCX WARN unexpected tag-receive descriptor ... was not matched. Rank 0 freed telemetry's communicator while a remote node's final node frame was still in flight; each sentinel now sends its node frame before its final rank frame (#447)
  • A run that can't listen on its telemetry port says so. Rank 0 logs telemetry can't listen on 127.0.0.1:<port> (<OS error>); this run has no telemetry stream. Pick another port with gempba::telemetry::configure_port., and the run goes on. Before, it went on with no stream and no message (#464)
  • On Windows, two runs no longer share a telemetry port. The server's SO_REUSEADDR let a second run bind a port in use, so both logged telemetry listening and every client reached only one of them. It now uses SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, so the second run warns as above; Linux and macOS keep SO_REUSEADDR, which there only allows rebinding a port left in TIME_WAIT (#464)
  • gempba-mpi no longer crashes the JVM when MPI runs over UCX. UCX puts its SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGILL and SIGFPE handlers in front of the JVM's and took the JVM's own deliberate SIGSEGVs for crashes, so every rank died within seconds: with Open MPI on its UCX PML, as on InfiniBand and RoCE clusters, and with MPICH over UCX, as Debian's is. On Linux, the native library now gives the JVM its handlers back; C++ programs keep UCX's (#443)
  • Java runs no longer crash with a SIGSEGV in gempba_create_explicit_node. The garbage collector could free a short-lived parent node, such as a dummy node, while native code was still copying it; the child factories and Node.getResult now keep it reachable (#452)
  • gempba_scheduler_destroy followed by gempba_shutdown deleted the scheduler twice. gempba_scheduler_destroy now frees only the handle (#414)

Build

  • GEMPBA_BUILD_MPI, on by default when gempba is the top-level project and off as a subproject, compiles the MPI component in gempba's own build, for its tests and the Java native, and needs MPI. Installs ship the component's source either way, so -DGEMPBA_BUILD_MPI=OFF builds and installs everything without MPI (#414, #415)
  • gempba's CMake build has one directory per component, src/core and src/mpi, each declared with one gempba_add_component() call from cmake/gempba_component.cmake. find_package loads each requested component through its installed gempba-<component>.cmake. The targets, options and installed files don't change (#436)
  • bindings/jni/build_deps.sh builds only hwloc's library and headers, not its command-line tools, so it no longer fails on hosts whose ncurses those tools can't link (#446)
  • macOS CI runs on Apple Silicon, and only on pushes to and pull requests into main and release, on v* tags and by manual run. The fat-JAR job fails unless each JAR holds exactly the three natives, and the Homebrew formulas are installed and tested on arm64 (#409)

Docs

  • The README describes the core and the MPI component: how each package installs, find_package(gempba COMPONENTS mpi), the MPI requirement, and macOS as aarch64 (Apple Silicon). Its Java section gives the Maven Central dependency and a Which MPI section on building gempba_jni against another MPI (#414, #415, #409, #410, #442)
  • Setting the telemetry port needs only <gempba/gempba.hpp>: call gempba::telemetry::configure_port(9001); before the first create_* call, as for gempba::telemetry::enable() and disable(); the default stays 9000. The C ABI's gempba_telemetry_configure_port and Java's GemPBA.configureTelemetryPort match it. No API changed: a test pins that the main header reaches it (#458)
  • docs/telemetry/wire-format.md documents the final line's end, the stop control line and the two dropped control lines (#465, #373)
  • docs/telemetry/custom-schedulers.md says what a custom scheduler implements for scheduler::run and what it does on a stop (#394, #465)
  • The Javadoc names the gempba and gempba-mpi artifacts instead of the mt and mp-mpi JARs (#470)

docs.title: v4.4.0
docs.text:
November 9, 2026

GitHub ↗

A packaging release. gempba's packages and Java JARs now install and build on a clean machine of each platform they support, instead of only on machines set up like the ones that built them. The Java natives depend only on the operating system and MPI, the public headers include only the C++ standard library, Windows moves from MSYS2's MINGW64 to UCRT64, and each package declares what it needs.

No public API is removed. Upgrading needs action in three cases: apt users switch the repository's suite from stable to noble, MSYS2 users install the UCRT64 packages, and a program that got spdlog or fmt through gempba's headers now finds them itself (see Changed).

Changed

  • The apt suite is noble. The .debs are built for Ubuntu 24.04, and the repository now publishes them in the noble suite instead of stable. In /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gempba.list, change stable main to noble main, then run sudo apt update; until then, apt update reports that the repository has no stable release. The repository serves the latest release, and older .debs stay attached to each GitHub Release (#411)
  • Windows uses MSYS2's UCRT64. MSYS2 is retiring MINGW64, so the packages are now mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gempba and mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gempba-mpi, installed from an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell. To build from the PKGBUILD, run MINGW_ARCH=ucrt64 makepkg-mingw -si. The Java DLL is built on UCRT64 too (#407)
  • The public headers include only the C++ standard library. gempba logs through functions compiled into the library and formats with std::format, so its headers no longer include spdlog or need fmt (#412):
  • spdlog is compiled into libgempba.a. The packages list it only as a build dependency, and gempba.pc no longer defines SPDLOG_HEADER_ONLY;
  • fmt stays a private link dependency, which find_package(gempba) still finds;
  • a program that used spdlog or fmt through gempba's headers now finds them itself, as gempba-examples does. If it also uses spdlog, it should use it header-only and at the same version, since libgempba.a holds its own copy of spdlog's inline code;
  • utils::log_and_throw and utils::print_ipc_debug_comments take a std::format_string. Calls with a literal format string compile unchanged.
  • The Java natives depend only on the OS and MPI. The C++ runtime, hwloc and fmt are linked into them, so they need glibc 2.28 or newer on Linux (such as RHEL 8), Windows 10 or newer, or macOS 14 or newer, plus an MPI runtime for mp-mpi. Before, they loaded only where the build machine's libraries were installed: MSYS2's DLLs on Windows, glibc 2.38 and Ubuntu 24.04's libraries on Linux, and Homebrew's fmt and hwloc and macOS 15 on Macs (#408)
  • Package descriptions call GemPBA a hybrid parallel framework (#411)

Fixed

  • find_package(gempba) works right after installing a package. gempbaConfig.cmake finds hwloc through pkg-config, but no package installed it, so on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 find_package(gempba) failed with "Could NOT find PkgConfig". libgempba-dev, the MSYS2 package and both Homebrew formulas now depend on pkg-config (#411)
  • The .deb declares the runtimes it needs: libc6 (>= 2.38) and libstdc++6 (>= 13.1), instead of libc6 (>= 2.17), which let it install on systems it can't link on. It no longer depends on libgomp1, which nothing used (#411)
  • The Homebrew formulas no longer install Boost, which gempba doesn't use (#411)
  • gempba builds with toolchains that lack std::stacktrace's library, such as Red Hat's gcc-toolset and macOS's clang. CMake links stdc++exp only where a std::stacktrace program links and otherwise builds without stack traces, and gempba.pc no longer names it (#408)
  • gempba compiles with the definitions of the spdlog package it finds, so an spdlog built against an external fmt no longer reaches for its bundled copy (#408)

Build

  • gempba compiles without MPI's C++ bindings (MPI_CXX_SKIP_MPICXX), since it uses only MPI's C API (#408)
  • The Linux JARs build in a manylinux_2_28 container (AlmaLinux 8, GCC 14) from bindings/jni/Dockerfile, so building them needs Docker and is x86_64 only. bindings/jni/build_deps.sh builds the static hwloc and the fmt and spdlog the natives link, from pinned, checksummed sources (#408)
  • scripts/check_jni_deps.sh fails a JAR build whose natives need anything beyond the OS and, for mp-mpi, MPI. On Linux it also fails a glibc floor above 2.28 (#408)
  • CI runs the Java tests on clean machines: on Linux in a stock Maven and JDK 25 container, and on Windows from PowerShell with no MSYS2 on PATH (#408)
  • Windows CI, the MSYS2 packages and build_jar_windows.sh build on UCRT64. The PKGBUILD builds for ucrt64 only, and build_jar_windows.sh refuses to run from any other MSYS2 shell (#407)

Docs

  • The README says what each package needs and where it runs: the .debs are for Ubuntu 24.04, the JAR needs Java 25, its macOS natives are Intel only, and the Requirements table lists every build dependency with its version (#411)

Not in this release

  • The Java JARs' macOS natives are still Intel only. Apple Silicon natives (#409), publishing to Maven Central (#410) and gempba in MSYS2's own repository (#413) move to v5.0.0.

docs.title: v4.3.0
docs.text:
November 6, 2026

GitHub ↗

A telemetry release about explaining scaling. When adding ranks stops making a run faster, telemetry now shows where the time went: pool threads idle because the rank has no work or because work isn't spreading, workers waiting on the coordinator, time spent moving tasks, and telemetry's own cost. Every run carries an id and describes its setup, and the dashboard can pause, snapshot and mark a run while it runs. Multiprocessing runs also end deterministically, without waiting out a timeout.

The telemetry JSON moves to schema 2, which renames and removes some keys; docs/telemetry/wire-format.md lists every change. C++ code built against v4.2.0 keeps compiling, with deprecation warnings where a call was renamed, unless it reads the telemetry frame structs directly or uses control_kind::SET_NODE_INTERVAL_MS (see Changed and Removed).

Added

  • Where idle time goes. Each rank splits its pool threads' idle time into idle_microseconds_starved, while no task runs anywhere in the rank, and idle_microseconds_imbalanced, while other threads run tasks. The two add up to idle_microseconds_per_thread. load_balancer gains get_starved_idle_time() and get_imbalanced_idle_time(), which return 0 unless a custom balancer overrides them (#337)
  • Scheduler state times. Workers report sched_running_microseconds and sched_waiting_microseconds, which together cover the run, plus first_task_ms and last_task_ms. The coordinator reports how long it takes to assign work (assign_latency_microseconds_total, assign_latency_microseconds_max, assign_count) and, under the centralized scheduler, available_microseconds_queue_empty: available ranks × time while its queue is empty (#338)
  • The coordinator's load, by kind. coordinator_state_msgs_total, coordinator_score_proposals_total, coordinator_score_broadcasts_total and, under the centralized scheduler, coordinator_full_microseconds. Every rank also reports telemetry_microseconds_total, telemetry's own time on the scheduler thread, so it isn't blamed on the scheduler (#339)
  • The cost of moving tasks. bytes_sent_total, bytes_recv_total, send_microseconds_total and recv_microseconds_total. telemetry_hub::record_send and record_recv take how long the MPI calls took, defaulting to zero (#340)
  • Spawn and score counters. spawn_rejected_pool_full and spawn_remote_rejected tell "work can't be handed over in time" apart from "the algorithm exposes little parallelism". Workers report score_proposals_sent, and the coordinator last_score_improvement_ms. load_balancer gains get_spawn_rejected_pool_full_count() and get_spawn_remote_rejected_count(), which return 0 unless overridden (#341)
  • A run id. Every broadcast carries run_id, a UUID v4, so a dashboard can tell two runs on the same port apart (#343)
  • The run's setup. The topology gains a run object: scheduler, load balancer, runtime mode, world size, threads per process, gempba_version, and annotations set with gempba::telemetry::annotate_run(key, value). Each rank's identity gains a role, "coordinator" or "worker" (#344)
  • Schedulers declare their roles and name. scheduler::role_of(rank) returns each rank's gempba::rank_role, and scheduler::get_name() names the scheduler in run.scheduler. The built-in schedulers make rank 0 the coordinator; a custom scheduler that declares nothing is "custom", with every rank a worker. role and threads_per_process follow these answers instead of assuming rank 0 is the coordinator (#391)
  • Pause and resume from the dashboard. {"kind":"pause"} stops every rank sending frames while counters keep counting, and the aggregator keeps sending a short "paused":true line so a paused run doesn't look lost. {"kind":"resume"} picks up at the same interval (#368)
  • Snapshots on demand. {"kind":"snapshot"} makes every rank send one frame right away, whatever the interval and even while paused, and the aggregator broadcasts one full line with them (#369)
  • Run markers. gempba::telemetry::mark_run("phase 2"), or {"kind":"mark","label":"phase 2"} from the dashboard, records a timestamped marker. Broadcasts list them under run.markers (#370)
  • A final line. The broadcast sent at shutdown says "final":true, and every other line "final":false, so a consumer can tell a finished run from a lost connection (#389)
  • coordinator_messages_handled in the MPI stats: every message the coordinator handled, 0 on workers. It reaches the C ABI and Java too (#342)

Changed

  • Schema 2. TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION is 2. Besides the added keys, schema 2 renames keys so each word means one thing: a rank is a process, coordinator and worker are scheduler roles, the aggregator (rank 0) serves the stream, and a thread is a pool thread. Update dashboards and scripts that read the old keys; wire-format.md keeps schema 1's names (#396, #342):
  • workers → ranks, worker_id → rank, the topology node's worker_ids → ranks, sentinel_worker_id → sentinel_rank, worker_local_ms → rank_local_ms;
  • idle_microseconds_per_worker → idle_microseconds_per_thread;
  • tasks_local_total → tasks_started_total, which counts every subtree handed to a pool thread, received ones included, at hand-off.
  • One telemetry interval. Node frames refresh with rank frames, and the aggregator broadcasts at that interval instead of every 500 ms, so one interval drives everything the dashboard shows. The control that sets it is {"kind":"set_interval_ms","value":N} (#345, #367, #396)
  • Deterministic MPI termination. Both MPI schedulers detect termination with Dijkstra–Scholten acknowledgements instead of a quiet period. A run ends as soon as its work is done, without the 3 s timeout at the end, and its result no longer depends on every message arriving within that timeout (#352)
  • Smaller rank frames. A rank frame carries only the destinations it sent tasks to: about 300 bytes instead of 16 KB, and destinations past rank 1,024 are recorded (#371)
  • C++ telemetry frame structs. Code that reads worker_frame or node_frame directly, such as a custom telemetry_transport or a caller of telemetry_hub::latest_rank_frame(), needs updating: m_tasks_local_total is now m_tasks_started_total, m_edges_out is a std::vector<edge_counter> holding only the destinations sent to, and the node frame no longer has m_net_aggregate or m_disk_aggregate (#342, #371)
  • The telemetry viewer. telemetry_view shows one row per rank with its role, marks paused stretches and prints run markers. The bash version now shows times on macOS too (#378)
  • The Java JARs' macOS natives are Intel only. They are built for osx-x86_64, while v4.2.0's were osx-aarch64, so on an Apple Silicon Mac the JAR finds no native to load. #409 tracks bringing Apple Silicon natives back (#387)

Deprecated

Each of these keeps working in v4.3.0 and is removed in v5.0.0 (#373, #353).

  • telemetry_hub::set_worker_interval_ms(), worker_interval_ms() and latest_worker_frame(), and control_kind::SET_WORKER_INTERVAL_MS. They forward to set_interval_ms(), interval_ms(), latest_rank_frame() and SET_INTERVAL_MS (#396)
  • telemetry_hub::set_node_interval_ms(), which does nothing, and node_interval_ms(), which returns the telemetry interval, since node frames follow it (#384)
  • The set_worker_interval_ms control line, which does what set_interval_ms does, and the set_node_interval_ms control line, which is accepted and ignored (#396, #367)
  • The total_requested_tasks stat. It means tasks sent plus received on workers, but requests handled on the coordinator. Read coordinator_messages_handled on the coordinator, and sent_task_count + received_task_count on workers (#342)
  • The scheduler timeout. create_scheduler(topology, timeout) in C++, gempba_scheduler_create in the C ABI and GemPBA.createScheduler in Java still take it, and ignore it (#352)

Removed

  • The telemetry_tunnel scripts and docs/remote-connection.md. The GemPBA Dashboard opens the SSH forward itself, including the jump-host hop and MFA (#378)
  • The node frame's net_aggregate and disk_aggregate. Both were always 0, and host network counters can't see RDMA or InfiniBand traffic. Use each rank's bytes_sent_total and bytes_recv_total for task traffic (#342)
  • control_kind::SET_NODE_INTERVAL_MS. Nothing outside gempba builds control messages, and the set_node_interval_ms control line is still accepted (#367)

Fixed

  • Every available rank gets work. The centralized coordinator's clear_buffer handed out at most one task per call; it now hands one to each available rank, highest priority first (#334)
  • Live idle time counts sleeping threads. A thread asleep through a starved stretch added no idle time until it woke, so live frames under-reported exactly while a rank was starved. End-of-run totals were already right (#335)
  • The last telemetry line is current. Shutdown publishes every rank's final frame before the last broadcast; under MPI the aggregator waits up to one second for them instead of dropping late ones (#336)
  • A slow client no longer stalls the telemetry stream. The aggregator wrote each line to every client in turn with blocking sends, so one client that stopped reading held up the other clients, the control lines and shutdown. Each client now has its own queue of up to 16 whole lines: a client that falls behind skips its oldest lines, and shutdown waits at most one second for it to take the final line (#69)
  • Workers read every coordinator notification before they exit. A worker told to terminate could leave score updates and other notifications unread before MPI_Finalize. The termination message now carries how many to expect, and each worker drains them (#356)
  • set_thread_pool_size returns once the pool is idle, so a try_local_submit right after it no longer sees a full pool (#348)

Build

  • The pinned thread pool is v5.1.0.3, in external/CMakeLists.txt and the Homebrew formulas. It counts sleeping threads' idle time and splits it into starved and imbalanced (#335, #337)
  • With GEMPBA_MPI_INTEGRATION_TESTS=ON, CTest runs termination_stress (both schedulers on 2, 4 and 8 ranks) and telemetry_stress (both schedulers on 4 ranks) under mpiexec. The Ubuntu CI job enables them (#352, #374)
  • CI runs on pull requests into any branch, not only main and release (#346)
  • The macOS jobs read the runner variable RUNNER_MACOS_INTEL instead of RUNNER_MACOS (#387)
  • The Homebrew verify job removes leftover gempba kegs before installing a flavor, and fails if one stays installed (#398)
  • CI runs fewer jobs per pull request:
  • each OS has one C/C++ test job, which publishes its own report, and one examples job that builds both flavors;
  • the .deb with its apt index, the MSYS2 package and the multi-platform JARs build only for pull requests into main or release and for pushes to them;
  • pull requests that change only docs or Markdown start no CI, and lint no longer runs on tags (#402)

Docs

  • docs/telemetry/wire-format.md describes the telemetry stream: every key with its unit and the release that added it, every control line, the compatibility rules and both schema versions (#381)
  • docs/telemetry/custom-schedulers.md says what a custom scheduler must do for its runs to reach the dashboard (#393)

docs.title: v4.2.0
docs.text:
June 16, 2026

GitHub ↗

A telemetry-on-real-clusters release. Watching a gempba run on an HPC compute node needs two things to be true at once: the per-node numbers have to be right, and you have to be able to reach them from your own machine. v4.2.0 delivers both — node telemetry now reports correct socket topology, CPU placement, and per-job memory on large multi-socket nodes, and the operator scripts can tunnel to a compute node through an MFA login node. The telemetry wire format only grows (additive cgroup-memory fields; schema version unchanged) and there are no public C++ API changes — additive on top of v4.1.3.

Fixed

  • Every node reports its real socket topology, not just the center. Per-host topology is now gathered with a variable-length collective — each host's sentinel serializes its own layout, exchanged via MPI_Allgatherv and merged by hostname — so all nodes report their sockets, cores, and full per-socket CPU lists (including wide sockets such as 96-core EPYC), instead of only rank 0's (#327)
  • Workers land on their real socket, and CPUs past index 64 are no longer dropped. The per-worker affinity bitmap grew from a single 64-bit word to a MAX_LOGICAL_CPUS-wide array, and each rank's primary socket is derived from its first allowed CPU through hwloc instead of being hardcoded to 0. On nodes with more than 64 logical CPUs this fixes the flat-zero per-allocation CPU% and the collapse of every rank onto socket 0 (#327)
  • Memory reflects the job, not the host. The node frame now carries the process's memory-cgroup usage and limit, resolved at the cgroup that actually enforces the allocation (scheduler-agnostic, cgroup v1 and v2), so a shared node shows gempba's own footprint against its allocation instead of the whole machine's memory. Falls back to host totals when the process is unconstrained (#327)

Added

  • Reach telemetry on a compute node through an MFA login node. telemetry_tunnel --jump-host nests the tunnel instead of using SSH ProxyJump: it forwards your machine to the login node, then runs the final hop on the login node so it rides the cluster's intra-cluster trust — one Duo prompt at the login node, no compute-node password, and gempba stays loopback-only. accept-new auto-trusts the per-job compute-node host key, and the readiness probe waits for a real byte rather than just a TCP accept. The mechanics are written up in docs/remote-connection.md (#325)
  • Bash ports of the operator scripts. scripts/telemetry_tunnel.sh and scripts/telemetry_view.sh join the PowerShell versions, so the tunnel and live-watch workflows run the same from Linux and macOS shells (#325)

Changed

  • The telemetry operator scripts were renamed and simplified. The helpers were renamed for clarity and the SLURM job-resolution path was dropped — pass the compute node directly (--ssh-host / --jump-host) instead of --job <slurm-id>. Update any wrappers that called the old names or relied on squeue resolution (#319)

Docs

  • Corrected the release dates in the per-version release notes (#323)

docs.title: v4.1.3
docs.text:
June 2, 2026

GitHub ↗

A telemetry-reachability release. Two fixes, both about getting at telemetry from outside the C++ runtime: C++ consumers can reach it through the umbrella header again, and the configure_port control is finally callable from the C ABI and Java. No runtime or scheduler API changes.

Fixed

  • gempba::telemetry::* is reachable through <gempba/gempba.hpp> again. The umbrella header didn't surface telemetry, so consumer code that included only <gempba/gempba.hpp> failed to compile gempba::telemetry::enable() with no member named 'telemetry' in namespace 'gempba' — and IDEs "fixed" it by inserting a deep, machine-specific include into the telemetry subheader. The umbrella now includes it, so the full public telemetry surface compiles from the one header consumers already use (#314)

Added

  • configure_port across the bindings. The telemetry kill switch (enable / disable / is_enabled) was already mirrored in the C ABI, JNI, and Java, but configure_port — the call that moves the telemetry TCP port off the default 127.0.0.1:9000 — had been left behind. It is now exposed as gempba_telemetry_configure_port (C ABI) and GemPBA.configureTelemetryPort(int) (Java, both flavors, with a 0..65535 range check). As in C++, call it before the first create_*: the hub captures the port once, when it installs (#315)

docs.title: v4.1.2
docs.text:
May 31, 2026

GitHub ↗

A targeted bugfix release: multiprocessing now runs on macOS. MP-mode binaries aborted at startup on macOS — and only macOS — with mutex lock failed: Invalid argument, while the same build ran fine on Linux and Windows. If you only use MT mode, or don't run on macOS, nothing here affects you. No library or API changes.

Fixed

  • macOS MP no longer aborts at startup. Both MPI schedulers passed a 128-byte buffer to MPI_Get_processor_name, which OpenMPI requires to be MPI_MAX_PROCESSOR_NAME (256) — it fills the full field, overflowing the buffer and zeroing an adjacent std::mutex. A zeroed mutex is a valid PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER on Linux/glibc, so the corruption stayed invisible there; macOS rejects it with EINVAL, so the first lock threw std::system_error. The buffer is now sized MPI_MAX_PROCESSOR_NAME in both the semi-centralized and centralized schedulers (#310)

Removed

  • Dropped an unused m_processor_name field from node_manager — declared but never read or written, and carrying the same undersized buffer (#310)

Docs

  • Added a DeepWiki badge and callout to the README (#308)

Build / CI

  • Split the Java binding workflow's native build from its tests, so a flaky Java test re-runs on its own without rebuilding the JNI library — the build job hands the native lib to the test job as a per-run artifact (#311)
  • Extracted the duplicated gempba-examples branch resolver into a shared composite action, deduping the three C/C++ CI workflows (#311)
  • Bumped the PKGBUILD sha256 for the v4.1.1 packaging artifact

docs.title: v4.1.1
docs.text:
May 30, 2026

GitHub ↗

A pure install-fixes release. v4.1.0 shipped the packages, but several of the documented install paths didn't actually work on a clean machine — the Homebrew build failed in the sandbox, the apt repo's signing key was never published, the MSYS2 download link pointed at a filename that doesn't exist. v4.1.1 makes every install command in the README work end-to-end, on all three platforms.

No library or API changes. If v4.1.0 already installed and built for you, nothing here affects your code — upgrade only if you hit one of the install problems below.

Fixed

  • brew install now works. The v4.1.0 formula died inside Homebrew's build sandbox — CPM/FetchContent tried to fetch BS_thread_pool over the network at build time, which the sandbox blocks. Those build deps are now vendored into the formula, so it builds offline (#288)
  • apt install no longer fails signature verification. The signed APT repo never exposed its public key, so apt update rejected it with NO_PUBKEY 7C5B392E…. The release now publishes the signing key (gempba-archive-keyring.gpg) alongside the index, so the documented signed-by= setup resolves (#286)
  • Dropped an unused OpenMP dependency the macOS formula pulled in for nothing (#289)

Docs

  • Rewrote the README's pre-built-package install instructions — every platform's block was broken or misleading (#286):
    • APT — added the one-time key-trust + repo-registration steps before apt install.
    • MSYS2 — the old releases/latest/download/<fixed-name> link 404'd (release asset names carry the version); now points at the Releases page + pacman -U.
    • Homebrew — fixed the literal <owner> placeholder, and clarified that both flavors install side by side (only one is linked at a time; each project points at $(brew --prefix gempba) / gempba-mpi).
    • Named the two flavors (mt / mpi / mp-mpi) up front so the section's recurring terms map to just two things.

Build / CI

  • The Homebrew formula is now built and brew test-ed on a real macOS runner on every PR and release, so a non-installable formula blocks the release instead of shipping (#292)
  • prepare-release bumps the Homebrew formula templates in lockstep with the other manifests — and actually stages them, so the bump lands on the prep branch (#297)
  • Hardened the macOS formula-verify job: pinned Homebrew off mid-run auto-update (which broke its ephemeral tap) and serialized the two-flavor matrix so they stop colliding on the shared prefix (#303)

docs.title: v4.1.0
docs.text:
May 28, 2026

GitHub ↗

Java. That's the headline.

gempba is now a Maven dependency. Drop it into a pom.xml, write import io.gempba.*, and call the same scheduler family, load balancer, and node manager you would from C++ — just from Java this time. One fat JAR per flavor (mt, mp-mpi) carries the native binaries for Linux, Windows, and macOS inside the artifact, so there is no per-platform build dance, no classifier juggling, no "first set LD_LIBRARY_PATH" footnote. You add the dependency, you build, you run.

That this is shippable at all is because of the second piece of v4.1.0: a stable C ABI underneath. The Java binding is the first consumer of it, but the same headers are what any future Python / Rust / .NET binding will sit on. If you have a JVM pipeline, a Spark job, an Airflow operator, an enterprise application — anywhere C++ was the wrong language but you still wanted gempba's scheduler — that bridge now exists.

Everything else in v4.1.0 is the surrounding work: the publish pipeline, the README the new Java audience needs, a couple of bug fixes. No public C++ API changes — additive on top of v4.0.0.

Added

  • Stable C ABI (<gempba/cabi/gempba.h>) — extern-C surface covering the full runtime: scheduler family, load balancer, node manager, factories, runnables, MP / MT entry points, per-node result retrieval. The same headers any non-C++ binding will reuse going forward (#185)
  • Java JNI binding (io.gempba:gempba) — typed wrappers for Node, LoadBalancer, NodeManager, RankStats, Score / ScoreType, Goal, BalancingPolicy, the task / serializer / deserializer functional interfaces, the scheduler family (MP-only), and GemPBA entry points for both flavors (#186)
  • Multi-platform fat JAR — each published JAR carries natives/<os>-<arch>/ for Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64, and macOS aarch64. NativeLoader picks the right binary at runtime, so the same JAR runs unchanged on any supported platform. No per-OS classifier, no platform-specific Maven profiles (#274)
  • Maven publication to GitHub Packages on every v* tag, with classifiers mt (multithreading) and mp-mpi (multiprocessing). Add the repo to your settings.xml, declare the dependency with the classifier you want, build (#187)
  • README "Maven dependency (Java)" subsection — repository + settings.xml + dependency snippet, plus a cutoff note that Maven artifacts start at v4.1.0 (earlier tags predate the publish flow). Platforms section gains a per-OS architecture table (#283)

Fixed

  • default_mpi_stats_visitor::labels() was missing the total_thread_requests key — values were emitted but the label vector didn't cover them, breaking downstream consumers that zipped labels with values (#262)
  • set_thread_pool_size could race against in-flight construction; the resize now round-trips a no-op task to fence the pool's worker threads before returning (#277)

Build

  • CI workflows split into mutually exclusive triggers: ci-*.yml runs on PRs and branch pushes, release-*.yml runs on tags. Reusable building blocks factored out so tag-time publish reuses the exact build path CI exercises (#265)
  • Workflow folder reorganized with ci- / release- prefixes, a .github/workflows/README.md, and shared composite actions extracted (#271)
  • prepare-release.yml now bumps bindings/java/pom.xml's <version> alongside the CMake / PKGBUILD bumps so the Java release version stays in lockstep with the C++ release version (#187)
  • Lint workflow bumped to LLVM 22; the modernizations clang-tidy 22 flagged were applied (#261)

docs.title: v4.0.0
v3.3.0
docs.text:
May 21, 2026

GitHub ↗

Runtime telemetry: process-wide hub with local / TCP / MPI transports, hwloc-backed topology probe, and a small set of read-only runtime accessors. Telemetry ships ON by default; opt out at runtime with gempba::telemetry::disable(). No API breaks.

Added

  • <gempba/telemetry/telemetry_hub.hpp> — process-wide telemetry hub that publishes worker / node frames and routes control messages. Singleton accessed via gempba::telemetry::get(); runtime kill switch via disable() / enable() / is_enabled() (process-local, sticky, must be set symmetrically across MPI ranks)
  • Local in-process and TCP server transports; TCP binds 127.0.0.1:9000 by default (configure_port() to change before the first create_* call)
  • MPI transport on a private communicator (MPI_Comm_dup) so telemetry traffic never collides with application traffic; auto-installed inside mp::create_scheduler so the collective install runs on every rank
  • hwloc-backed topology probe: per-socket physical / logical core counts, total memory, CPU brand, cpu-id list; multi-node topology assembled via MPI_Allgather of the worker_identity POD
  • JSON serializer for telemetry frames; client-pushed interval-control protocol over the TCP socket so dashboards can throttle publish rate live
  • Read-only runtime accessors: gempba::try_get_scheduler (non-throwing variant of get_scheduler), load_balancer::get_thread_pool_size, load_balancer::get_tasks_running_count, scheduler::get_pending_request_count
  • scripts/connect_telemetry.sh — SSH-tunnel helper for inspecting a remote rank's telemetry socket from a local dashboard

Changed

  • Default thread-pool size when no explicit size is set is now 1 (was one-per-core via BS::thread_pool's default). The concrete quasi_horizontal_load_balancer and work_stealing_load_balancer impls construct BS::thread_pool<>{1} explicitly. Users who relied on the implicit default should pass the size explicitly through their scheduler init

Fixed

  • Exported gempbaConfig.cmake now re-discovers hwloc behind GEMPBA_HWLOC, so downstream find_package(gempba) consumers resolve PkgConfig::HWLOC at link time instead of failing with target not found (latent since hwloc became a PRIVATE link dep on a STATIC library)
  • mpi_semi_centralized_scheduler double-counted m_sent_task_count — increments fired on two paths for the same dispatch; consolidated to a single ownership point so the stats visitor and telemetry's record_send see consistent values

Build

  • hwloc is a new runtime dependency, gated by the GEMPBA_HWLOC CMake option (ON for releases, OFF for dev builds). Discovered via pkg-config on all three platforms; .deb and MSYS2 packages declare it as a runtime dep
  • CI installs hwloc on Ubuntu 24.04 / macOS 26 / Windows 2025 (MSYS2) / lint runners
  • build_*.sh scripts forward GEMPBA_HWLOC so packagers can disable hwloc cleanly
  • Windows builds link psapi (process-info probe) and ws2_32 (Winsock for the TCP server)

docs.title: v3.2.0
docs.text:
May 21, 2026

GitHub ↗

CI hardening and release-flow automation. No library API or behavior changes.

Fixed

  • publish-apt-repo no longer depends on the GitHub CLI being on the runner image — it consumes the .deb from the same workflow's artifact instead of gh release download, so self-hosted Linux runners can publish on tag pushes again

Build

  • BS::thread_pool pinned to release tag v5.1.0.1 instead of tracking master for reproducible builds
  • CI clang-tidy bumped from 18 to 19; bugprone-throwing-static-initialization enabled — debug_logger_initializer's ctor is now noexcept with the spdlog calls wrapped in try/catch, preserving the static-init injection contract while making it honest
  • update-pkgbuild.sh accepts -r / --remote to select which git remote's tag to hash against (defaults to origin); useful when cutting a release pointed at the public repo
  • New Prepare release workflow (workflow_dispatch): branches prep/v<version> from the resolved target branch, bumps CMakeLists.txt + packaging/msys2/PKGBUILD, drafts docs/releases/release-notes-v<version>.md from git log, and opens the prep PR. Auto-detects the target branch (or accepts a target_branch input / vars.RELEASE_TARGET_BRANCH override) so the same workflow runs on forks with only main and on forks with both main and release
  • New Post-tag PKGBUILD sha256 cleanup workflow (push tags: v*): replaces the prep PR's 'SKIP' placeholder with the real sha of the source tarball; opens a follow-up PR. Auto-resolves the target branch via tag-commit reachability when both main and release exist
  • New set-release-body job in c-cpp-ubuntu.yml: applies the curated docs/releases/release-notes-v<tag>.md to the GitHub Release body via gh release edit --notes-file; fails loudly if the notes file is missing so no tag ships without curated notes
  • New setup-gh-cli composite action: pinned gh on PATH for self-hosted Linux runners; no-op on github-hosted runners where gh is pre-installed

docs.title: v3.1.1
docs.text:
May 19, 2026

GitHub ↗

Post-v3.1.0 hygiene release: packaging metadata, coverage scope, CI workflow polish, a test-coverage push, cross-platform fixes, and toolchain bumps. No public API changes.

Changed

  • gempba::create_custom_node now takes a std::shared_ptr<node_core> directly (no more wrapping at the call site)
  • wall_time reimplemented on top of std::chrono (replaces gettimeofday) — same observable values, monotonic clock semantics
  • gempba::log_and_throw marked [[noreturn]] so static analyzers and the compiler's flow analysis understand the call never returns
  • score: cleaned up the kind / to_raw / from_raw paths and added explicit unreachable markers
  • node_core_impl: lazy-init and result paths consolidated; redundant explicit destructor on node removed; excessive debug logging trimmed
  • Codebase-wide clang-tidy identifier-naming pass (private members and locals only — no public API renames)

Removed

  • Dead prune() overload in work_stealing_load_balancer
  • Unreachable defensive checks in get_root_level_pending_node

Fixed

  • gempba::utils::get_nb_set_bits signed-char overflow on MinGW
  • MSYS2/MinGW build: <windows.h> is now included before <psapi.h> so psapi.h sees the types it needs
  • centralized_utils.hpp: NOMINMAX redefinition guarded so headers that already define it don't trigger a warning
  • node.hpp: <stacktrace> inclusion gated on the __cpp_lib_stacktrace feature test, not just __has_include

Build

  • MSYS2 PKGBUILD sha256 updated to match the v3.1.0 source tarball
  • Codecov reporting now excludes examples/, tests/, and external/ so coverage numbers reflect only library code
  • New clang-tidy and clang-format identifier-naming and configuration rules so future changes can't reintroduce the patterns just cleaned up
  • Ubuntu CI bumped to GCC 14; <stacktrace> and stdc++exp linkage gated accordingly so older toolchains still build the library
  • macOS CI defaults to the macos-26 runner image
  • Self-hosted runners are now matched by label set (multiple labels combined) rather than a single label
  • MS-MPI runtime installed on the Windows CI runner so the multiprocessing test set actually runs
  • clang-format diagnostics surfaced with the colored summary; lint.sh diagnostics made readable on the terminal
  • Skip the publish-test-results job when the upstream build was cancelled
  • runs-on injected from vars.RUNNER_* repository variables so runner targets can change without editing each workflow
  • New full-coverage tests for the gempba facade, node_manager, quasi_horizontal_load_balancer, work_stealing_load_balancer, node_core_impl, centralized_utils, plus branch coverage for queue, utils, score, and node
  • Thread pool readiness ordering tightened in throw/discard tests so the send() race no longer deflakes them
  • Dropped flaky peak-vs-current RSS comparisons from the memory-usage tests
  • -Wunused warnings silenced on header-only helpers

April 19, 2026

GitHub ↗

macOS support, system packaging (.deb, MSYS2, signed APT repo), and cross-platform portability fixes.

Breaking changes

  • gempba::Queue renamed to gempba::queue (header moved to include/gempba/utils/queue.hpp) — update any direct uses
  • Bundled spdlog removed; consumers must now provide a system-installed spdlog (and fmt) via find_package

Added

  • macOS officially supported (Apple Silicon, AppleClang/libc++, Homebrew Boost 1.90)
  • Debian/Ubuntu .deb packages (libgempba-dev) published on tagged releases
  • Signed APT repository at apt-repo/ with pubkey.gpg for apt-get install libgempba-dev
  • MSYS2 PKGBUILD at packaging/msys2/ for mingw64 / ucrt64 / clang64 builds, with a Windows CI publish job producing .pkg.tar.zst artifacts
  • CMake install rules and gempbaConfig.cmake — consumers can now find_package(gempba 3.1.0 REQUIRED) and link gempba::gempba

  • -rdynamic is now applied only on Linux Debug builds (no longer leaks into Release or non-Linux targets)
  • CPM.cmake download hardened against silent corruption

Fixed

  • mpi_centralized_scheduler: misplaced parenthesis in the MPI_Wtime/diff_time comparison broke the rate-limit on "center queue full" notifications, causing repeated worker contacts every loop iteration instead of at most once per second
  • <bits/stdc++.h> removed from node_manager.hpp — header now compiles on libc++ / AppleClang / MSVC
  • C++23 <stacktrace> gated on __has_include so libc++ targets without it still build
  • gempba::score type-dispatch, comparison, and to_string made portable across long double ABIs

  • BS_thread_pool include directory now propagated so private headers compile against installed packages

Removed

  • Private node_manager method that always returned zero (worker view returns zero directly)

docs.title: v3.0.0
docs.text:
December 7, 2025

GitHub ↗

The largest release in the project's history: a ground-up redesign that replaces the heavy template-driven API with a single-header gempba:: facade. branch_handler becomes node_manager, the entire pre-v3 surface (result_holder, dynamic_load_balancer_handler, Pool, args_handler, all *2-suffixed members) is removed, and the public surface is reorganized under include/gempba/.

Breaking changes

  • gempba::branch_handler renamed to gempba::node_manager (class and header) — the main user-facing class
  • gempba::ResultHolder / gempba::result_holder removed entirely; use gempba::node instead — function signatures no longer take a holder template
  • gempba::DLB_Handler / gempba::dynamic_load_balancer_handler removed; use gempba::load_balancer (interface) and the new create_load_balancer factories
  • gempba::Pool and gempba::args_handler removed
  • All *2-suffixed members removed: is_done2, wait2, get_balancing_policy2, plus *2 variants in MPI schedulers
  • node_manager::lock() / unlock() removed
  • node_manager member renames: try_push_mp → try_remote_submit, try_push_mt → try_local_submit, force_push → force_local_submit, push_multiprocess / push_multithreading → send, WTime → get_wall_time, try_top_holder → try_push_root_level_holder_remotely, pass_mpi_scheduler → pass_scheduler
  • Identifier renames on the public surface: load_balancing_strategy → balancing_policy, print_mpi_debug_comments → print_ipc_debug_comments, FUNCTION_ARGS → TASK, gbitset → G_BITSET, "reference value" → score throughout MPI schedulers
  • mpi_scheduler renamed to mpi_semi_centralized_scheduler
  • scheduler members supplanted by scheduler::worker / scheduler::center views: fetch_solution, fetch_result_vector, next_process, push, run_node, run_center, try_open_transmission_channel, close_transmission_channel
  • scheduler::get_total_requests removed (now sourced from the new stats interface)
  • C++23 enforced in CMake (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23, CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON, extensions off); C++20 compilers are no longer supported
  • BS::thread_pool is now an external dependency; consumers using CPM mirror it automatically, manual integrations must add it
  • GEMPBA_* compile definitions on the gempba target are now PRIVATE instead of PUBLIC
  • Public headers reorganized under include/gempba/ (core/, utils/, stats/, defaults/, detail/); legacy include/utils/... paths are gone
  • Legacy .csv / .dat raw printing removed from examples; CSV log is now opt-in and off by default

Added

  • Single-header facade #include <gempba/gempba.hpp> exposing gempba:: factories
  • gempba::node — lightweight, copyable, template-free node handle (replaces result_holder)
  • gempba::shutdown() for explicit, controlled global cleanup
  • gempba::node_manager factories: multithreading::create_node_manager(load_balancer*) and multiprocessing::create_node_manager(load_balancer*, scheduler::worker*)
  • gempba::load_balancer public interface with two stock implementations: quasi_horizontal_load_balancer (recommended) and work_stealing_load_balancer
  • multithreading::create_load_balancer(balancing_policy) and multiprocessing::create_load_balancer(balancing_policy, scheduler::worker*) factories, plus a BYO-implementation overload
  • gempba::scheduler public interface with scheduler::worker and scheduler::center views, scheduler_traits, and multiprocessing::create_scheduler(scheduler_topology, timeout) (SEMI_CENTRALIZED, CENTRALIZED)
  • gempba::node_core extension point (include/gempba/core/node_core.hpp) plus node_traits and the detail/nodes/node_core_impl.hpp template implementation
  • gempba::stats and gempba::stats_visitor interfaces; default_mpi_stats_visitor for the bundled MPI schedulers (visitor pattern, string-keyed metrics)
  • gempba::serial_runnable interface with serial_runnable_void / serial_runnable_non_void impls and runnables::return_none::create / runnables::return_value::create helpers for MP task dispatch
  • gempba::serializable interface to split serialization responsibilities out of node trace
  • gempba::task_bundle and gempba::transmission_guard utilities under include/gempba/utils/
  • invokable C++23 concept that enforces task signatures of the form Ret(std::thread::id, Args..., node)
  • gempba::score extended with uint32_t and int64_t so it can carry std::size_t and other common types; spaceship operator<=> on task_packet
  • utils::log_and_throw (replaces direct spdlog::throw_spdlog_ex) with C++23 <stacktrace> integration
  • Generated gempba/config.h (from config.h.in) so IDEs see the build flags
  • Multi-processing and multi-threading benchmark cases
  • One-call Windows and Linux build scripts and helpers to run all graphs in a directory

Changed

  • Module renames swept the codebase to snake_case: BranchHandler → branch_handler (then node_manager), ThreadPool → thread_pool, DLB → dynamic_load_balancer, MPI_Modules → schedulers, Resultholder → result_holder (then removed)
  • gempba::score now has unsigned 32/64 specializations; score::make(...) accepts std::size_t
  • Schedulers now receive their timeout at construction (create_scheduler(topology, timeout))
  • default_mpi_stats_visitor lives in the defaults module and is exposed via multiprocessing::get_default_mpi_stats_visitor()
  • Internal spdlog::info calls demoted to spdlog::debug
  • #ifdef GEMPBA_DEBUG_COMMENTS replaced with #if GEMPBA_DEBUG_COMMENTS (matches the new cmakedefine01)
  • README rewritten for v3.0 (facade pattern, extensible architecture, updated requirements, Windows added to supported platforms)

Fixed

  • Race condition that could let a worker thread throw
  • Edge case in node pruning (children weren't cleared on prune)
  • Critical guard fix in quasi_horizontal_load_balancer

Build

  • C++23 enforced (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON, CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
  • Links stdc++exp on non-MSVC for C++23 <stacktrace> support
  • New GEMPBA_DEV_MODE toggle in the root CMakeLists.txt (auto-on when gempba is the root project)
  • GEMPBA_* target flags scoped to PRIVATE (no longer leaks to consumers)
  • BS::thread_pool added via CPM (rapastranac/thread-pool); argparse moved to examples/external since it's only used by examples
  • GIT_SHALLOW TRUE set on CPM external clones
  • Per-test discovery in CTest (gtest_discover_tests) and a separate test-artifact publish job in CI; FLAKY_ test-name convention for flaky cases
  • Dropped redundant git install step from CI

docs.text:
September 1, 2025

GitHub ↗

Single-fix patch release for the centralized MPI scheduler.

Fixed

  • mpi_centralized_scheduler worker probe_reference_value_comm() was probing REFVAL_PROPOSAL_TAG (the worker-to-center tag) instead of REFVAL_UPDATE_TAG, so global reference-value updates broadcast by the center were never picked up by workers — leaving them with stale bounds and exploring branches that should have been pruned (#55)

docs.title: v2.1.0
docs.text:
August 23, 2025

GitHub ↗

Source-level Windows support, alongside a dedicated Windows CI pipeline.

Added

  • Windows build support: GemPBA now compiles on Windows with MSVC
  • run.ps1 PowerShell launcher at the repo root for running multiprocessing (mpiexec.exe) and multithreading example binaries on Windows
  • Windows CI workflow (.github/workflows/c-cpp-windows.yml) building on Windows Server 2022, with a matching status badge in the README

Changed

  • centralized_utils.hpp now defines NOMINMAX, WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN, and RPC_NO_WINDOWS_H before including windows.h to avoid std::byte ambiguity and min/max macro clashes against <windows.h>
  • score::make factory dispatches by integral size (int32_t/int64_t) instead of exact type, so scores constructed from long and other platform-dependent integer widths behave the same on Windows and Linux
  • Ubuntu workflow renamed from c-cpp.yml to c-cpp-ubuntu.yml (Ubuntu 24.04); README badge updated accordingly
  • args_handler.hpp switched to angle-bracket includes and replaced std::forward<nullptr_t>(nullptr) with a plain nullptr argument for portability

Fixed
